explanation: Think of the epididymis as a training ground! Newly made sperm aren't ready to swim yet; they spend time here resting, maturing, and learning how to swim. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which atom in the human body is primarily targeted during an MRI scan?

options.A: Hydrogen
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Carbon

explanation: Because the body has so much water, hydrogen protons are abundant and react strongly to the MRI magnetic field. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why must medical waste be burned in an incinerator or buried deep instead of going to a normal dump?

options.A: It is required to generate electricity for local hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for any kind of protective clothing
options.C: It prevents injuries and the spread of infectious pathogens
options.D: It turns hazardous waste into edible organic fertilizer

explanation: Well done! Hospital waste carries germs and sharps that can easily harm waste workers and the community if not safely destroyed. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which topical preparation is best suited for treating thick, dry, and scaly skin lesions?

options.A: A watery lotion
options.B: An oil-based ointment
options.C: A fast-drying powder
options.D: An alcohol-based liquid

explanation: Ointments have a heavy oil base that traps moisture and softens hard, thick, scaly skin much better than water-based creams or lotions. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why does a crashing patient make standard IV drug delivery so difficult?

options.A: The skin becomes too thick for any needle to pierce
options.B: The blood begins to flow backward toward the feet
options.C: Emergency drugs are blocked by the skin's natural oil barrier
options.D: Peripheral veins flatten and collapse, making them hard to cannulate

explanation: When blood pressure drops severely, peripheral veins empty out and flatten. This makes slipping an IV cannula in super tough during an emergency! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which test measures the exact number of HIV particles floating in the blood?

options.A: Viral load test
options.B: Basic metabolic panel
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: CD4 cell count

explanation: A viral load test counts how many copies of the virus are in the blood sample. Spot on! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h6)

question: Where should you position the steam generator in relation to the patient's bed?

options.A: Underneath the mattress for hidden warmth
options.B: Tied securely to the side rail of the crib
options.C: At a safe distance to prevent accidental burns
options.D: Directly inside the tent canopy next to the pillow

explanation: Safety first! Always keep the hot generator far enough away to protect the patient from burns. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h3)

question: What major problem must nurses watch out for after an infant goes through a difficult resuscitation?

options.A: Permanent closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.B: Hypoglycemia and temperature instability
options.C: Sudden onset of infantile colic
options.D: Excessive weight gain over the first day

explanation: Resuscitated babies burn through their sugar reserves very quickly and have a hard time staying warm, so checking blood sugar and temperature is vital. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h7)

question: What three things are checked when using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?

options.A: Temperature, respiration, reflex movement
options.B: Pupil reaction, blood pressure, heart rate
options.C: Swallowing, grip strength, speech clarity
options.D: Eye opening, verbal response, motor response

explanation: Remember the big three for GCS: how they open their eyes, what they say, and how they move their body! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of recording moulding on the partograph during labour?

options.A: To measure the strength and frequency of maternal uterine contractions
options.B: To detect early signs of mechanical obstruction or tight pelvis
options.C: To determine the exact volume of amniotic fluid remaining in the uterus
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the fetus before delivery

explanation: Moulding is tracked on the partograph primarily to catch signs of difficult labour and cephalopelvic disproportion early. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h4)

question: Where do the ovarian arteries originate from directly?

options.A: Femoral artery
options.B: Superior vena cava
options.C: Abdominal aorta
options.D: Renal vein

explanation: The ovarian arteries branch directly off the descending abdominal aorta high in the abdominal cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC)?

options.A: Treating sudden life-threatening pregnancy complications
options.B: Monitoring normal fetal growth during the third trimester
options.C: Providing routine antenatal counseling and vitamins
options.D: Assessing nutritional status prior to conception

explanation: You've got this! EmOC is all about handling sudden, dangerous emergencies during labor, delivery, and after birth to save both mother and baby. Great job! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of involving local residents in data collection?

options.A: It allows nurses to stay inside the office all day long
options.B: It builds local ownership and trust in health programs
options.C: It forces community members to pay taxes to the clinic
options.D: It removes the need for professional nursing training

explanation: When residents participate in the diagnostic process, they value the resulting health interventions and support them willingly. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which cancer is linked to advanced HIV and caused by human herpesvirus 8?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Acute myeloid leukemia
options.C: Cervical carcinoma
options.D: Kaposi sarcoma

explanation: You've got it! Kaposi sarcoma causes distinct purple or brown skin lesions and can affect internal organs in advanced HIV. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h7)
